Test whether two alternatives can be combined

Source: R/tests_fit.R
combine_test.Rd

Tests the hypothesis that two alternatives are indistinguishable with respect to the covariates: all coefficients other than the constants are equal in the two equations (when one of the two is the base, that the other's coefficients are zero). The Wald form uses the fitted covariance; the likelihood-ratio form (Cramer and Ridder 1991) refits the multinomial logit with the two alternatives pooled and adds the binomial constant-only log-likelihood of the split within the pooled alternative: \(\ell_R = \ell_{pooled} + n_j \log(n_j/n_{jk}) + n_k \log(n_k/n_{jk})\). Both are chi-square on the number of non-constant terms (Stata's mlogtest, combine and lrcomb): the restriction leaves the two constants free, through the pooled equation's constant and the split share. An alternative that is never chosen contributes \(0 \log 0 = 0\).

Usage

combine_test(object, alternatives = NULL, type = c("wald", "lr"))

Arguments

object

A fitted mnl() model (for the LR form: case-specific covariates only, in either layout, and every alternative available; the Wald form works for any multinomial-logit fit).

alternatives

Two alternatives (labels). NULL (default) tests every pair.

type

"wald" (default) or "lr".

Value

A data frame of class "iia_test" with one row per pair: pair, statistic, df, p.value.

Details

The likelihood-ratio form under separation and penalties:

  • For a maximum-likelihood fit of separated data it compares the suprema of the log-likelihoods (see lr_test()).

  • For a penalized fit (firth = TRUE or a prior) it is the penalized likelihood ratio, the restriction imposed on the full model's penalized log-likelihood (no pooled refit).

The likelihood-ratio form assumes independent cases (a fit's cluster does not enter it); the Wald form uses the fit's covariance, cluster-robust when the fit has one.

References

Cramer, J.S. and Ridder, G. (1991). Pooling states in the multinomial logit model. Journal of Econometrics, 47, 267-272. doi:10.1016/0304-4076(91)90102-J

Long, J.S. and Freese, J. (2014). Regression Models for Categorical Dependent Variables Using Stata, 3rd ed. Stata Press.

See also

term_test(), iia_tests()

Other specification tests: captivity_test(), hl_test(), rank_test(), term_test()

Examples

set.seed(1)
## alternatives b and c share their slopes
d <- rmnl(1000, beta = cbind(b = c(0.5, -1, 0.8), c = c(0.3, -1, 0.8)))
m <- mnl(y ~ x1 + x2, data = d)
combine_test(m)
#> Test of combining alternatives (Wald) 
#>   pair statistic df p.value
#>  a & b   137.974  2  <2e-16
#>  a & c   110.967  2  <2e-16
#>  b & c     1.839  2   0.399
combine_test(m, c("b", "c"), type = "lr")
#> Test of combining alternatives (likelihood ratio, Cramer-Ridder) 
#>   pair statistic df p.value
#>  b & c     1.845  2   0.397
